reply_text:
I read through the whole repo (version 1.12.0: about 8 small source files, 2 test files and 3 sample posts). Adding a feed is a small change, but the codebase has a few rules a feed could easily break, so I've built the plan around them.

## Rules from the codebase the feed must follow

1. **No dependencies at all.** `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` says sites copy the whole folder into their own repo and run it with plain node. So no feed library: we write the RSS 2.0 XML by hand, the same way `src/sitemap.js` does.
2. **Skip drafts and scheduled posts.** The samples include a draft (`notes`) and a post held until 2027-01-15 (`launch`). The feed must use the same `isPublished(post, now)` filter, with the same `now` passed in from `build()`. A feed that showed an unreleased post would be a real leak, because feed readers keep everything they fetch. (A recent commit, "Sitemap lists only published posts", fixed exactly this bug for the sitemap.)
3. **Base path and stable URLs.** Sites are often served under a subpath like `https://example.test/blog`. A test comment says every absolute link must go through `absoluteUrl()`, and that permalinks never change. Feed links and GUIDs should be `absoluteUrl(site, permalink(p))`, never put together by hand.

## Plan

**1. New `src/feed.js`** exporting `feed(site, posts, now = Date.now())`:
- Filter with `isPublished`. Sort newest first by `publish_at`, because `loadPosts` sorts oldest first by filename. Cap at about 20 items, configurable.
- Channel fields: `title`, `link`, `description` (fall back to the title), `lastBuildDate`, and `<atom:link rel="self">` pointing to `absoluteUrl(site, '/feed.xml')`.
- Each item: `title`, `link`, `guid isPermaLink="true"` (same as the link, so it never changes), `pubDate`, and `author` from `site.author`.
- Dates: RSS needs RFC 822 format, and `new Date(p.publish_at).toUTCString()` gives that with no library.
- Escaping: escape every text field. `escapeHtml` already covers `& < > "`, which is enough for XML text; it might be worth adding a `'` case or a small `escapeXml` alias. Put the post body in `<description>` as escaped HTML. Note that `build.js` drops the raw body into the page with no markdown conversion, so the feed would carry exactly what the page shows. Avoid CDATA, because a body containing `]]>` breaks it.

**2. Wire it into `src/build.js`:** add `out['/feed.xml'] = feed(site, posts, now);` next to the sitemap line.

**3. Help readers find it:** add `<link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml" href="…/feed.xml">` to the page output. Right now pages are just `<h1>` plus the body, with no `<head>`, so this goes in wherever head markup lands first. Also mention the feed in the README.

**4. Fix the dev server (also an existing bug).** `src/devserver.js` adds the `<script>` live-reload snippet to every response. That would corrupt `feed.xml` and already corrupts `sitemap.xml` locally. It should only add the snippet to `.html` responses and set the right `Content-Type`, `application/rss+xml` for the feed. Similarly, `minify()` should never run on XML output.

**5. Tests in `test/feed.test.js`**, using a fixed `now` like the existing tests:
- Only `hello-world` appears; `notes` (draft) and `launch` (scheduled) don't.
- With `now` after 2027-01-15, `launch` appears, newest first.
- Links and GUIDs keep the `/blog` base path, even when `baseUrl` ends with a trailing slash.
- Titles containing `&` or `<` are escaped, and dates are in RFC 822 format.
- A check that `package.json` dependencies are still empty.

## Questions for you
- Should the feed carry **full post text or just a summary**? I'd default to full text, with an optional `feed.summaryOnly` setting.
- **RSS only, or Atom too?** RSS 2.0 is enough for nearly every reader, and Atom would be about 30 more lines.
- **What should `feed.xml` contain when nothing is published yet?** I'd output a valid channel with no items.

I haven't changed anything in the repo. Once you've answered these, I can build it.
